title: Set the break-glass accounts (operator route)
purpose: Replaces the list of break-glass (emergency) accounts that PIM Manager never disables, revokes or offboards, writing it straight to the environment's store with a justification; for when the normal two-person route in PIM Manager cannot be used.
whenToRun: Only when the Manager's own route (one SuperAdmin requests, a second approves) cannot work: an environment with a single SuperAdmin, or a Manager that is down while an emergency account must be protected now. PIM Manager points the only SuperAdmin to this script.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins), signed in through the browser or the Invardia Support app session (no Azure CLI)
runAs.why: The list lives in pim.Settings and every write is audited; only the SQL admin group may write it. With -UseSignedInAccount the signed-in az user is used. Alternatively the admin application's certificate (-AdminAppId + -AdminCertThumbprint), or a ready -ConnectionString to a local SQL Server.

changes.object: pim.Settings row 'BreakGlassAccounts' (the complete list of UPNs / object ids)
changes.scope: this environment: PIM Manager and its engine
changes.why: Accounts on the list are exempt from every disable, revoke and offboard PIM does. Written compare-and-set against the list just read, then read back.
changes.undo: Run the script again with the previous list (it is printed as 'stored now' at the start of every run).

changes.object: pim.AuditEvents event 'breakglass.accounts.set' (actor, ActorSource 'setup', justification, added and removed accounts)
changes.why: Every change to the emergency list is audited with who and why.
changes.undo: None -- the audit trail is append-only by design.

changes.why: For a caller that reads the outcome.

parameters.name: Accounts
parameters.help: The COMPLETE new list (UPNs and/or object ids). It replaces the stored list.

parameters.name: Justification
parameters.help: Why -- recorded on the audit event.

parameters.name: ConfirmEmpty
parameters.help: Required to store an EMPTY list (it removes the protection from every emergency account).

parameters.name: ConnectionString
parameters.help: A ready connection string to the store (e.g. a local SQL Server with Integrated security) instead of -SqlServer.

parameters.name: SqlServer
parameters.help: The store's server (alias -SqlServerFqdn). An Azure SQL FQDN connects with a token.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id; required for an Azure SQL store.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Reach the store as the signed-in az user (a member of the SQL admin group). The recommended way.

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Automation: the admin application's client id (with -AdminCertThumbprint).

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation: the thumbprint of the admin application's certificate in the local machine store.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the outcome as JSON to this file.

readsOnly: pim.Settings 'BreakGlassAccounts' (the stored list and its snapshot hash; a store that cannot be read is not written)
the PIM Manager's open break-glass change request, if any (reported: it will be refused as stale after this write)
whatIf: Validates the entries, reads the stored list, prints what would be added and removed, 'What if: Performing the operation "replace the break-glass account list with: <accounts> (audited as 'breakglass.accounts.set')" on target "pim.Settings['BreakGlassAccounts'] in <server>/<database>"' and 'What if: would store N account(s) ...'. Nothing is written and no audit event is recorded.
undo: Run the script again with the list it printed as 'stored now' and a justification. The audit events stay.
